I farm this maize plot like my father taught me. I have no school learning, but I know my land — almost one hectare of maize here, and I put beans between the rows like always. The rains in Iringa are usually good, so I do not need to buy much. I keep some cattle and goats, so I carry their manure to the plot before planting — that is what I trust. Fertilizer from the shop costs too much money I do not have, and my neighbors who tried it say one bag is not enough for a whole plot anyway. I save seed from last year's harvest, the same maize we have grown for many seasons. My wife and grown children help me weed and harvest, and at planting time I call two or three young men from the village for a few days when the work is heavy.
